blocks.text: 1. Image Classification
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445476497-919884532.png

ConvNeXt, the final topic of the previous CNN Architectures module, closed out coverage of complete network designs. Image Classification opens the Computer Vision Tasks module, the genuinely foundational task those designs were built to solve.
It assigns a single label to an entire image, the genuinely simplest visual task covered throughout this topic and the module it opens.

https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445476497-297590536.png

This connects back to Feature Maps and Flattening, both already covered in the CNN module. Given one entire image, produce exactly one predicted class label, a genuinely simple, direct task specification.

This is a genuinely direct application of everything already covered throughout the CNN and CNN Architectures modules, with the entire pipeline already covered there feeding into this exact final prediction task.
3. Recapping The Architectures Built For This Task
This connects back to every architecture already covered throughout CNN Architectures. LeNet through ConvNeXt were all genuinely designed and evaluated primarily on this exact task.

Image Classification, already covered as this topic's own definition, is the genuinely foundational Computer Vision Task, the exact benchmark every architecture covered in that previous module was measured against.

blocks.text: 4. Recapping The Output Layer

This connects back to Softmax, already covered in the Activation Functions module. The final layer genuinely outputs a probability for every possible class, exactly the mechanism already covered there.
The genuinely highest probability class becomes the network's own predicted label, a direct, familiar decision rule already covered throughout earlier topics in this course.
5. The Single-Label Assumption
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445476497-7088858.png

A genuinely important, real assumption connects back to Loss Functions, already covered in its own module. Standard Image Classification genuinely assumes exactly one correct label per image, matching Cross-Entropy Loss's own standard use already covered there.

This is a genuinely important, real constraint worth naming explicitly, since some real images genuinely contain multiple valid subjects, a limitation revisited further in this module's own later topics.
6. Top-5 Accuracy
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445476497-842371297.png

This connects back to Accuracy, already covered in the Evaluation Metrics module. A genuinely useful, related metric, Top-5 Accuracy, counts a prediction correct if the true label is among the 5 genuinely most likely predictions.

This is a genuinely more forgiving metric for tasks with many, genuinely similar candidate classes, where the single top prediction alone, already covered as plain Accuracy, might unfairly penalize genuinely reasonable near-misses.

blocks.content: Top-5 Accuracy, already covered in this topic, became especially common for large-scale Image Classification benchmarks with hundreds or thousands of candidate classes, where several genuinely plausible labels can reasonably apply to the same image.

A genuinely important, real practical shortcut connects forward to Transfer Learning, covered later in this course. A network already trained for Image Classification often transfers genuinely well to other, related tasks.

This genuinely valuable property, explored in complete depth in that later module, means the effort invested training on Image Classification, already covered throughout this topic, rarely goes to waste.
8. A Genuine Limitation Of This Task

blocks.alt: A Genuine Limitation Of This Task
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445604375-870190723.png

A genuinely honest limitation connects forward to Object Detection, covered in the very next topic of this module. Image Classification genuinely says nothing about where within the image an object actually is.
This genuinely real gap, a single label with no spatial location attached, is exactly the limitation that the very next topic in this module directly addresses.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Plain Image Classification Is Genuinely Sufficient

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Plain Image Classification Is Genuinely Sufficient
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445604375-660636879.png
A single, genuinely dominant subject filling most of the image is a direct case where Image Classification, already covered in this topic, directly answers exactly what that subject is.
Needing genuinely fast, simple predictions without spatial detail is another genuine case where Image Classification's own genuinely simple output, already covered, keeps inference genuinely fast.
10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates a genuinely simplified Image Classification pipeline, computing class probabilities via Softmax and reporting both Top-1 and Top-5 predictions, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
class_names = ["cat", "dog", "bird", "fish", "horse", "rabbit", "deer", "fox", "bear", "wolf"]

logits = rng.normal(size=len(class_names))  # already covered as the final layer's raw output

def softmax(x):
    exp_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x))
    return exp_x / exp_x.sum()

probabilities = softmax(logits)  # already covered as Softmax, recapped in this topic
sorted_indices = np.argsort(probabilities)[::-1]

print("Top-1 prediction (already covered as the final decision rule in this topic):")
print(f"  {class_names[sorted_indices[0]]}: {probabilities[sorted_indices[0]]:.3f}")

print("\nTop-5 predictions (already covered as Top-5 Accuracy in this topic):")
for idx in sorted_indices[:5]:
    print(f"  {class_names[idx]}: {probabilities[idx]:.3f}")

blocks.content: Running this example shows the single Top-1 prediction alongside the broader Top-5 predictions, exactly the two decision granularities already covered in this topic for evaluating Image Classification performance.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Image Classification assigns a single label to an entire image.
It is the foundational task every architecture in CNN Architectures was designed and evaluated on.
The final layer uses Softmax to output a probability for every possible class.
Standard Image Classification assumes exactly one correct label per image.
Top-5 Accuracy counts a prediction correct if the true label is among the 5 most likely predictions.
A network trained for Image Classification often transfers well to other, related tasks.
It says nothing about where within the image an object actually is located.
Next up: Object Detection, which addresses exactly that limitation by locating individual objects.
